title: TPS continuity probe: cross-variant throughput fingerprinting
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Goal: Build and maintain a tokens-per-second (TPS) microbenchmark called the 'continuity probe' that produces deterministic throughput fingerprints for our core model family (small/med/large, quantized variants). This harness focuses on steady-state throughput, p95 token latency tracking, and lightweight regression detection that integrates with CI and our observability stack.

Background: Existing TPS tests capture peak throughput but are noisy across minor infra changes and don't highlight gradual p95 drift across model variants or quantization profiles. The continuity probe will standardize traffic patterns, sequence lengths, KV cache states, and batching strategies so we can compare exact fingerprints across commits and runtime releases.

Scope:
- Design a reproducible steady-state runner with configurable ramp, microburst injection, and prefix-cache warmup.
- Collect tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99, and token-level tail latency along with resource counters (GPU util, memory, host CPU).
- Implement lightweight regression detector that triggers alerts on relative TPS drop >= 7% or p95 increase >= 12% compared to baseline.
- Integrate with CI (nightly & premerge smoke) and Cloudwatch/Prometheus dashboards for long-term drift charts.
- Provide simple artifact output (CSV + json-lines) and a canonical diff tool for fingerprints.

Out of scope: full-blown sustained throughput CI for Dedicated pools (handled in ENG-121057) and adversarial traffic fuzzing (future work).
acceptance_criteria: Continuity probe can execute 30m steady-state runs for small/med/large variants with configurable sequence length distributions
Collected metrics include TPS, token-level p50/p90/p95/p99, and GPU/CPU/memory counters stored to S3 and visible in dashboard
Regression detector produces a deterministic pass/fail with thresholds configurable per-model and emits a CI artifact with fingerprint diffs
Nightly job in CI runs the probe and historical drift appears on the throughput-observability dashboard for 7+ days
Developer docs and quickstart: how to run locally, interpret fingerprints, and open a regression investigation ticket

notes_and_decisions: Decision: Use relative thresholds (pct change) instead of absolute TPS to accommodate hardware variance across Dedicated hosts
Decision: Baselines are per-model-version + quantization profile and stored as compressed fingerprint blobs in S3 (proto -> jsonlines for human readability)
Trade-off: We will run 30m steady-state windows in nightly CI; shorter premerge runs (3m) will be used for quick feedback to avoid long PR cycles
Implementation note: leverage existing microbench harness components from ENG-5931 where possible but avoid copying test patterns that caused flaky p95 in the past
Scope note: We intentionally exclude integration with rollout auto-fallbacks in this ticket; follow-up will add automated rollback triggers
